correctness.rationale: PASS: Haar normal directions on the simplex affine span are centered Gaussian scores G_i centered by their mean and divided by independent R. An invariant affine offset conditional on hitting the body has width-weighted direction measure; R-independence gives exactly the Gaussian-range-weighted threshold representation. Every generic simplex section vertex corresponds to an edge with one endpoint on either side, giving N=k(m-k). Integrating admissible threshold intervals yields P{N>=r(m-r)}=E G_(m-r+1)/E G_(m); summing edge crossing intervals gives mean m(m-1)/(2 sqrt(pi) mu_m). For fixed q<1/4 choose r=ceil(rho_q m); empirical normal quantiles give z_q/mu_m and the claimed 1/sqrt(logm) rate. Range/(2 sqrt(2logm))→1 in L1 makes width-weighted and ordinary Gaussian samples asymptotically total-variation close; uniform threshold fraction V yields s/b_m→2V−1, Gaussian tail counts give log N/logm→2−(2V−1)^2. Independently verified quadrature tail probabilities, exact mean-via-edge identity for m=3,4,5,6,9, and tetrahedral balanced probability 0.288535543072. Finite checks do not establish the distributional limits.

originality.rationale: PASS: Kabluchko–Litvak–Zaporozhets (2016/2017) give Gaussian range/mean-width and its extreme-value asymptotics, but not Crofton-conditioned section crossing-edge counts; these are acknowledged input. Brandenburg–De Loera–Meroni (2023) optimize section combinatorics but do not give invariant affine section probability. Previous published central-simplex section laws fix the offset at the centroid and have different chi-square rather than broad affine threshold behavior. None of the inspected exact prior statements implies the order-statistic survival law, random exponent and rare balanced coefficient without further new analysis.
